properties.description: A narrow forest trail approaches a rocky hillside. The path is worn, partly concealed by undergrowth, and marked by faint goblin trail signs. The main camp entrance is close by.

environment.smell: pine, damp earth, faint wood smoke

properties.description: A broad irregular crack in the rock, partly hidden by bushes and loose stones. Crude tripwires, warning marks, and the smell of smoke mark it as goblin territory.
Tall trees, thick undergrowth, moss, mushrooms, and animal trails dominate this forest. The canopy keeps the light dim. It is ideal goblin territory: full of food, danger, and hiding places.
A natural underground pool fed by a slow seep. The water is cold, clear, and extraordinarily valuable. The goblins fill skins, barrels, and pots here.
The largest cave chamber. A central fire burns low, surrounded by stones, crude tables, bones, and hanging meat. This is where the tribe eats, argues, and listens to the chief.
A river cutting through the eastern territory. It provides fish, clay, driftwood, and a travel corridor. Humans follow it, and so do goblins, which makes it both useful and dangerous.

Crumbling dwarven stonework, broken tools, old mechanisms, and scattered metal litter these ruins. They are a major source of scavengable materials, but they may still contain traps, unstable passages, or residual dangers.
Rocky hills north of the camp. Stone, iron ore, caves, goats, and hidden paths are found here. The terrain is rough and offers both shelter and exposure.
A wide dirt road connecting Eldenford to larger towns. Travelers, carts, merchants, and patrols use it. Goblin scouts watch from cover, looking for profitable opportunities.

A deserted human farm southeast of the camp. Old grain, vegetables, tools, barrels, rope, nails, wood, furniture, cloth, and chicken coops remain. Rats nest in the buildings. The goblins raid it repeatedly.
A broad, swampy lake southwest of the camp. Reeds, dead trees, islands, and stagnant pools cover the shoreline. The water is murky. Fish, frogs, snakes, and rare plants are found here.
A downstream chamber where refuse, bones, ash, and rotten material are dumped. It is not hygienic by human standards, but it is positioned so water carries some waste away from the living areas.
Hammocks, furs, blankets, and piles of leaves are scattered across the floor. Personal weapons, scraps, lucky objects, and stolen trinkets litter each sleeping spot.
A smaller chamber overlooking part of the settlement. Better furs, trophies, weapons, and stolen objects are heaped here. The walls bear crude victory markings.
Broken swords, bent nails, wire, rope, gears, springs, glue, pitch, and scrap metal cover the tables and shelves. This is where things are taken apart and made to do something else.
Crude maps are scratched into leather, bark, stone, and parchment. They mark patrols, trails, berry patches, dangerous monsters, and loot. The maps are practical, not geographic.
A chamber kept for the smallest goblins. Low hammocks, fur piles, broken toys, sticks, stones, and scattered tools create a chaotic but supervised space.
A rough open chamber used for sparring, weapon practice, and trap avoidance training. The floor is scuffed, the walls are dented, and the noise level is almost always high.

The shaman's chamber feels different from the rest. Symbols, bones, feathers, painted stones, strange plants, and relics cover the walls. Shelves hold herbs, potions, powders, and objects nobody else is allowed to touch.

environment.smell: herbs, smoke, something sweet and wrong

properties.description: Large fires, hanging pots, meat racks, and drying racks dominate this chamber. Smoke coats the walls. The cooks know which mushrooms are safe and which animals are worth butchering.

a wooden rocking horse with a faded red leather saddle. it rocks gently as you pass, though no one touched it. one of its painted eyes seems to follow you. the rockers creak rhythmically, slowly coming to a stop.

a porcelain doll with cracked, vacant eyes that seem to stare directly through you. its dress is old-fashioned, lace-trimmed. one arm is broken, revealing the hollow porcelain interior. something is stuffed inside.

a tiny scrap of paper that was hidden inside the broken doll: 'the skull is in the study. take it to mother's grave. she'll know what to do. — e.' the handwriting is a child's, but the message is clear.

lead toy soldiers arranged in a battle formation around a tiny replica of a crystal skull, made from painted glass. the soldiers point their rifles at the tiny skull, as if trying to protect something from it.

a child's leather diary, the pages yellowed and crumbly. the recurring phrase, written over and over in different colors of ink: 'the skull watches. the skull waits. eleanor is lonely. she wants me to play with her but she's not real anymore. mother says don't go near the study. but the skull calls me at night.' the final entry: 'tonight she's going to show me how to fly.'
a small music box with a dancing ballerina. when opened, it plays a haunting, beautiful lullaby. the tune is strangely soothing, and as it plays, the whispers in the walls seem to harmonize with it.
a small wooden bed with a faded quilt patterned with stars and moons. the pillow is dented. the sheets are cold, but they smell faintly of lavender soap.
A rusted hatchet with a loose handle.
A crude goblin spear with a sharpened tip.
A heavy wooden club.
A shattered wooden shield, barely held together by straps.
A crude snare trap that has been sprung and broken.
A strip of tough dried meat.
A handful of mushrooms. Some look edible. Some look suspicious.
A handful of wild berries.
A length of coarse rope.
A wooden torch wrapped with cloth, ready to be lit but currently unlit.
an old oil lantern hanging from a nail by the stairs. empty, but the wick is intact. if you had oil, it would work perfectly.

a half-full plastic water bottle. lukewarm but clean.
an old kettle. it's empty but the spout still whistles faintly when you touch it, as if echoing a sound from another time.

a rusty watering can. empty. when you pick it up, something rattles inside — a small object.
a nightstand glass with stale but drinkable water. a ring of sediment circles the bottom.
rows of rusted meat hooks hanging from the ceiling. they clink together softly, though there's no breeze.
an empty rack that once held butcher's tools. only one remains — and it's in the butcher's hand.
A stone fireplace, cold and dark. A pile of ash sits in the hearth. A poker rests against the hearth, waiting to stir the embers.

a tall wooden wardrobe containing moth-eaten coats and a single man's suit. in the pocket of the suit: a train ticket stub, dated october 31st, 1891. the return portion is unused.

a wooden vanity with a cracked, spotted mirror. a silver hairbrush and jewelry box sit on it, exactly as they were left. the mirror reflects strangely — your image seems to move a split second after you do.

Worn, leather-bound notebook with tattered pages, stuffed with loose papers, charcoal rubbings, pressed desert flowers, and notes. Covers are scarred, binding loose. When not in use, it's tucked into a pocket. Always within reach.

sealed cardboard cases of hard taco shells on the storage shelf, stamped with a January best-by date that management recycles out of rotation every inventory.

A worn leather satchel, slung over one shoulder and perpetually overstuffed with everything Lyrie might need—and a great deal she doesn't. The strap has been tied and re-tied where it snapped. Contents spill out constantly: pressed flowers, lost buttons, half-eaten apples, crumpled notes, a broken comb, and at least three rocks she thought were 'pretty.' The flap never stays closed.

Old brass telescope, tarnished with age. Hairline crack in the lens but still functional. Acquired from a dead soldier near the Galtian border. Worn on a leather cord around the neck or tucked into a pocket.
an old wooden crib with a threadbare blanket. a worn stuffed rabbit lies inside, one button eye missing. the crib rocks slightly on its own.

a small wooden toy box in the corner, painted with fading circus animals. the lid is heavy. inside: a collection of old toys, all broken or damaged. a doll with no head. a horse with no legs. a jack-in-the-box that won't open.
A thick wooden club wrapped in leather at the grip. Heavy, crude, and devastating when it connects.
A rusted hatchet with a loose handle.
You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel. A flask burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern.
a large butcher knife on the counter, still sharp after all these years. the blade is pristine — recently cleaned.

A compact crossbow, meticulously maintained and loaded with a single bolt. The wood is darkened with age, but the string is taut and the mechanism is clean. It looks effective, if only you had a clear shot.
A heavy wooden club.

a stone altar draped in dusty black cloth. a shallow depression in the shape of a skull sits at its center, lined with faded runes. this is where the crystal skull belongs — the altar in the crypt, just as the journal said. when placed here, it might break the curse... or seal it forever.
A small iron charm shaped like a sunburst, warm against the palm. It steadies the heart against fear.
a human femur bone lying on the floor near a shattered sarcophagus lid. it's old and brittle.
a small obsidian pendant miki bought at a spiritual shop. she claims it wards off evil spirits.
scattered bones on the floor — some animal, some human. one skull has a neat hole drilled through the crown.
a brass compass in the desk drawer. the needle doesn't point north — it points toward the fireplace, no matter where you stand. there must be something magnetic behind it.

a stone sarcophagus bearing the name 'augustus blackwood (1835-1891)'. the lid is heavy but slightly ajar. scratch marks — long, desperate scratch marks — cover the inside of the lid. he was buried alive.
rows of rusted meat hooks hanging from the ceiling. they clink together softly, though there's no breeze.
A stone fireplace, cold and dark. A pile of ash sits in the hearth. A poker rests against the hearth, waiting to stir the embers.
a large oak barrel. it smells strongly of vinegar — whatever wine was in here has long since turned. but the barrel itself is solid, and the iron bands are intact.
Strips of dried, salted meat hanging from hooks. They look preserved and edible.
A heavy iron cauldron sits on the stove, filled with cold, thick soup.
a massive meat cleaver, its blade stained dark with old blood and rust. the weight of it speaks of years of brutal work.
a dried apple core someone left here decades ago. brown and shriveled, not edible.
a bagged order abandoned in the pickup shelf, going lukewarm under the heat lamp. the receipt curling at the edge says NO ONE HAS COME FOR THIS in the language of forgotten food.
A strip of tough, salted meat. It's edible, if not exactly gourmet.
